messages.subject: a problem with crossbar (moving to ggplot0.9)
parts:
Dear All,

I am struggling with the ggplot2_0.9 in order to reuse my previous code. I asked Had for an help and he suggests me to post again my request to the list (trying to provide a reproducible example). Here it is. 

Sorry for posting again the question, I try to better explain my problem.


The following code worked perfectly for me on a linux system with ggplot2_0.8.5 on an older R version:


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

library(ggplot2)

library(MASS)


stat_sum_single <- function(fun, geom="point", colour="red", size=3, ...) {

   stat_summary(fun.y=fun, colour=colour, geom=geom, size=size, ...)

}


stat_sum_crossbar <- function(fun1, fun2, fun3, geom="crossbar", colour="blue", ...) {

   stat_summary(fun.y=fun1, fun.ymin=fun2, fun.ymax=fun3, colour=colour, geom=geom, ...)

}


carsRidotto <- subset(Cars93, Passengers %in% 4:6)

ggp <- qplot(data= carsRidotto, Passengers, Price, geom="point")

ggp2 <- ggp + stat_sum_single(mean, shape=8, size=8)

ggp2 <- ggp2 + stat_sum_single(function(x) quantile(x, 0.1), colour="orange", shape=17, size=7) +

    stat_sum_single(function(x) quantile(x, 0.9), colour="orange", shape=17, size=7)

ggp2 <- ggp2 + stat_sum_crossbar(function(x) quantile(x, 0.5),

                                 function(x) quantile(x, 0.25),

                                         function(x) quantile(x, 0.75),

                                         geom="crossbar", colour="blue", width=0.5)

ggp2


ggp3 <- ggp2 +

stat_quantile(colour="blue", size=1, linetype=2) +

stat_quantile(colour="orange", size=1, linetype="twodash",quantiles=c(0.1, 0.9)) +

stat_smooth(method=lm, se=FALSE, colour="red")

ggp3


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Here you can find the three resulting graphs:


http://stat.unicas.it/downloadStatUnicas/appoggio/fig-ggp.pdf

http://stat.unicas.it/downloadStatUnicas/appoggio/fig-ggp2.pdf

http://stat.unicas.it/downloadStatUnicas/appoggio/fig-ggp3.pdf


and here is my sessionInfo():


http://stat.unicas.it/downloadStatUnicas/appoggio/sessionInfo.txt



Using the last version of ggplot2 on a Mac OsX installation, I have problem with the second plot. Here is my new sessionInfo()

http://stat.unicas.it/downloadStatUnicas/appoggio/sessionInfoNew.txt


In particular here is the resulting "bad" plot:


http://stat.unicas.it/downloadStatUnicas/appoggio/bad-fig-ggp2.pdf


The third plot correctly adds the regression lines to the second plot (I think the problem lies in the stat_sum_crossbar function). Here is the "bad" third plot:


http://stat.unicas.it/downloadStatUnicas/appoggio/bad-fig-ggp3.pdf


Thanks to the help of Brian Diggs, I succeed in reproduce the ggp2 plot using the group aesthetic in the qplot, i.e. as follows:


ggp <- qplot(data= carsRidotto, Passengers, Price, geom="point", group=Passengers)


but using such change I am not more able to reproduce the third plot.


I really appreciate any suggestion.


Ciao,

domenico

parts:
Hi Domenico,

This works. The group aesthetic fixes it. This works:

ggplot(carsRidotto,aes(Passengers,Price))+
geom_point()+
stat_summary(fun.y ="mean",colour="red",size=4,shape=8,geom="point")+
stat_summary(fun.y = function(x) quantile(x,.9), colour="orange", shape=17, size=7, geom="point")+
stat_summary(fun.y = function(x) quantile(x,.1), colour="orange", shape=17, size=7, geom="point")+

stat_summary(aes(Passengers,Price,group=Passengers),fun.y = function(x) quantile(x,.5), fun.ymax = function(x) quantile(x,.75)
                ,fun.ymin = function(x) quantile(x,.25)
                ,width=0.5,geom="crossbar",colour="blue")+

stat_quantile(colour="blue", size=1, linetype=2) +
stat_quantile(colour="orange", size=1, linetype="twodash",quantiles=c(0.1, 0.9)) +
stat_smooth(method=lm, se=FALSE, colour="red")

Adam Loveland
